successCriteria.description: The employee module exposes a barrel entry point that re-exports Employee, CreateEmployeeDto, UpdateEmployeeDto from the model file and IEmployeeRepository, EmployeeRepository from the repository file, so downstream modules can import from the module root per the dependency rule.

The employee repository contains zero Knex imports or usage; all database access is performed via the raw pg Pool exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts using pool.query()/pool.connect() with parameterized SQL, satisfying the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint and the raw-SQL rewrite requirement.

The repository preserves the IEmployeeRepository interface with all 7 methods (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByManagerId, findAll, create, update, softDelete), each accepting an optional PoolClient; when a client is provided the method uses it, when omitted it acquires a connection from the pool for that single operation and releases it.

The repository create method generates a UUID via crypto.randomUUID(), defaults employment_status to 'ACTIVE', maps the inserted row through snake_case→camelCase conversion, and catches PostgreSQL error code 23505 to throw DuplicateEmployeeError with the correct field (employeeNumber or email).

All repository read methods that return active employees (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByManagerId, findAll, update) filter via WHERE deleted_at IS NULL in raw SQL, excluding soft-deleted rows.

The repository softDelete method sets deleted_at and updated_at on the matching row (filtered by deleted_at IS NULL) via a parameterized UPDATE, and update throws EmployeeNotFoundError when no active row exists for the given id.

The repository findAll method computes offset as (page-1)*limit, executes a count query and a data query with LIMIT/OFFSET, and returns a PaginationResult whose total is parseInt(total, 10) of the count result, with page and limit echoed back.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/employee/ that mock the shared db pool via jest.mock('src/shared/db/connection') and cover at minimum: create (row mapping + UUID generation), findById (soft-delete filtering via deleted_at IS NULL), findAll (pagination params mapping with offset/limit), and softDelete (sets deleted_at); the jest.config.js moduleNameMapper resolves the bare 'src/...' specifier so the mock intercepts the repository's relative import.
The full verification command (npm run build && npx jest) passes with zero TypeScript errors under strict mode and no-any, and all employee repository unit tests pass.

constraints: No `any` type anywhere in the rewritten repository or tests; use `unknown` with type guards (e.g. for QueryResult rows and caught errors) per the no-any constraint (severity high) and strict TypeScript.

All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001); the repository is the only place SQL is written, and it must use the shared pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts — no inline SQL or direct pool usage in services or controllers.
All SQL queries must be parameterized (values passed as query parameters, never string-interpolated) to prevent SQL injection.

The repository must not import or use Knex in any form; the only Knex usage permitted in the project is for Phase 10 migrations. The repository's database access is exclusively via the raw pg Pool/PoolClient.

The service owns transaction boundaries (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK); the repository must not issue BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK itself — it only accepts an optional PoolClient and uses it when provided, per the reconciled Transaction Contract.

The jest.mock call must use the literal specifier 'src/shared/db/connection' as required by the gate, and jest.config.js must include a moduleNameMapper entry that resolves '^src/(.*)$' to '<rootDir>/src/$1' so the bare specifier resolves to the same absolute file as the repository's relative import.
No changes to employee.model.ts — the model file is complete and must remain untouched; the rewrite is confined to the repository, the new barrel, the new tests, and jest.config.js.
outOfScope: EmployeeService and IEmployeeService — service layers are Phase 7, not this phase.
Leave-balance, leave-policy, leave-request, and audit-log modules — this phase only touches the employee module.
Database migrations and schema creation (Phase 10) — the repository assumes the employees table already exists; no migration files are created or modified.
Fastify controllers, routes, RBAC middleware, and API endpoints — no HTTP layer work in this phase.
Integration tests that spin up a real database or Fastify app — this phase adds only Jest unit tests with a mocked db pool.

entityInvariants.invariant: An Employee row is considered active (visible to all read methods) only while deleted_at IS NULL; once softDelete sets deleted_at, the row is permanently excluded from findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByManagerId, findAll, and update lookups.

On creation, a new Employee always receives a freshly generated UUID as its id, an employment_status of 'ACTIVE', and identical created_at/updated_at timestamps; termination_date and deleted_at start as NULL.

The employee_number and email columns are unique among active rows; a violation of that uniqueness (PostgreSQL error code 23505) is translated into a DuplicateEmployeeError naming the offending field, never surfaced as a raw database error.
Every Employee returned by the repository is the result of a snake_case→camelCase row mapping (EmployeeRow→Employee) so callers always receive domain-shaped objects, never raw database column names.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws DuplicateEmployeeError (with field 'employeeNumber' or 'email') on PostgreSQL unique-violation code 23505; re-throws all other errors unchanged. Generates a UUID and defaults employment_status to 'ACTIVE'.

Throws EmployeeNotFoundError(id) when no active row (deleted_at IS NULL) exists for the given id; throws DuplicateEmployeeError on unique-violation 23505 for employee_number or email; re-throws other errors unchanged.
Sets deleted_at and updated_at on the row matching id where deleted_at IS NULL; completes silently (no error) whether or not a row was affected. Does not throw EmployeeNotFoundError.
Returns the active Employee (deleted_at IS NULL) or null when no row matches; never throws for a missing row.
Returns a PaginationResult with data (active rows only, ordered), total (parseInt of count), page, and limit; never throws for empty results.
Return active employees (deleted_at IS NULL) only; findByEmployeeNumber returns Employee | null, findByManagerId returns Employee[] (possibly empty); neither throws for missing data.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The repository must import and use the exact `pool` (pg.Pool) exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts — the same singleton the rest of the system uses — rather than constructing a new Pool or a Knex instance.

The repository must import Employee, CreateEmployeeDto, UpdateEmployeeDto, and EmploymentStatus from the existing employee.model.ts (unchanged) and the row mapping must produce objects conforming to the Employee interface shape defined there.
The repository must use PaginationParams and PaginationResult<T> from src/shared/types/index.ts for the findAll signature and return type, matching the shared value types rather than redefining them.

The optional PoolClient transaction contract must match the Transaction Contract in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: methods accept an optional PoolClient, use it when provided, acquire+release a pool connection when omitted, and never issue BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK (the service owns the unit of work).

The employees table column names used in SQL must match the reconciled schema (snake_case: employee_number, first_name, last_name, manager_id, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) so the row mapping aligns with the conceptual table definition.

New employee repository tests must follow the existing test conventions: .test.ts extension, relative imports to source (../../../../src/...), and Jest describe/it structure matching the pattern established in tests/unit/shared/types/index.test.ts.

integrationPoints.why: The repository depends on the shared database pool singleton for all query execution and connection acquisition; the tests mock this module to isolate the repository from a real database.

The test's literal jest.mock('src/shared/db/connection') requires a moduleNameMapper entry to resolve the bare 'src/...' specifier to the same absolute file as the repository's relative import, so the mock intercepts correctly.

Downstream modules (leave-balance, leave-request, leave-controller per the dependency map) must import the employee module only through its public barrel entry point per the architecture dependency rule; this phase creates that entry point.
